unit.title: Clinical Office Practice and Patient Safety

sections.learningObjectives:
- Support specimen collection and labeling by preparing supplies, identifying patients with two identifiers, and labeling at the point of collection in accordance with policy and supervision.
- Document specimen collection accurately and verify specimens against orders and patient identity before transport.
- Recognize specimen integrity problems and escalate issues to appropriate staff following office policy and the chain of command.
- Apply standard precautions and bloodborne pathogen safety practices when handling, transporting, and disposing of specimens and sharps.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

The assistant is like a helper in a science lab who gets the cups and labels ready and follows the teacher's exact steps, but the teacher decides what experiment to run and reads the results.

### Question 2

Just like you check both a name tag and a birth date before handing someone their package, two matching facts are needed to be sure the right person is giving the sample.

### Question 3

Label the cup the moment you fill it, like writing a name on a birthday present right after wrapping it so gifts do not get mixed up.

### Question 4

The label is like a luggage tag that has the traveler's full name, the date, and who packed it, so the bag always gets back to the right person.

### Question 5

Put the name tag on the lunch box, not on the lid that might be thrown away or switched with someone else's.

### Question 6

It is like catching someone putting name tags on empty lunch boxes before lunch; the safe thing is to speak up and fix it before the wrong food goes in the wrong box.

### Question 7

It is like picking the right-size container for leftovers; if you use the wrong one, the food (or sample) might not keep properly for testing.

### Question 8

Mix it the way you gently turn a snow globe upside down a few times, not the way you shake a juice bottle hard.

### Question 9

It is like following a recipe that says fill the cup to the line; too much or too little changes how the mixture works.

### Question 10

It is like pouring different flavors into cups in a set order so the last flavor does not leave a taste that ruins the next drink.

### Question 11

It is like reminding someone to come with an empty stomach for a test and asking to be sure they did, then writing down their answer so the team knows.

### Question 12

It is like checking whether someone is allergic to a food before cooking, so you can use a different ingredient and keep them safe.

### Question 13

Wash your hands before and after touching samples, just like washing before and after cooking, so germs do not spread.

### Question 14

Gloves are like oven mitts for your hands; they are the basic protection you put on before touching something that could be messy or harmful.

### Question 15

Carry the sample in a sealed bag, like carrying soup in a sealed container so it cannot spill on the way.

### Question 16

Some foods must be kept in the fridge and some on the counter; follow the specific rule for each sample so it stays good for testing.

### Question 17

It is like teaching someone to wash their hands and let the water run a moment before filling a clean cup, so only the clean middle part goes in.

### Question 18

It is like starting a timer: pour out the first bit, then save every drop into the big jug for one whole day and night.

### Question 19

It is like telling someone to use the special little scoop so only the sample goes in the cup, not the water it was sitting in.

### Question 20

You want the deep cough from the chest, like clearing your throat really well in the morning, not just spit from your mouth.

### Question 21

It is like a relay race where each runner signs a paper when they pass the baton, so you can prove exactly who had it at every step.

### Question 22

Write down the who, what, when, and where of the sample, like a receipt that proves what happened and when.

### Question 23

Double-check that the name on the cup matches the name on the order form, like making sure the right homework has the right student's name.

### Question 24

Check two matching facts both when the sample goes in and when you get it back, like checking a name and birthday at both the start and end of a task.

### Question 25

If a sample looks spoiled, do not pretend it is fine; raise your hand and tell the grown-up so it can be redone the right way.

### Question 26

It is like a receipt; if there is no record, it is hard to prove what happened.

### Question 27

Fix a mistake by drawing one neat line through it and writing the fix with your initials, like correcting a paper without ripping the page out.

### Question 28

Never say a job was done when it was not; be honest and tell the person in charge so the right thing happens.

### Question 29

It is like a sign-out sheet that shows who borrowed the sample and whether it made it to the lab.

### Question 30

When something is marked urgent, move it to the front of the line carefully, like handling a rush order without skipping any safety checks.

### Question 31

Some measurements change by the hour, so writing down the exact time is like stamping a time on a photo to know when it was taken.

### Question 32

Write down whether the person really followed the no-food rule, because the answer changes what the numbers mean.

### Question 33

It is like noting whether a photo was taken with a wide or zoom lens; the way you got it changes how you read it.

### Question 34

It is like scanning a library book to make sure the right book goes on the right shelf without spelling errors.

### Question 35

Your job is to make the sample match the doctor's list, not to add or remove items from the list yourself.

### Question 36

If you cannot read the instructions, ask the person who wrote them instead of guessing, like asking the teacher what the assignment says.

### Question 37

If the order says a sample from the left side, take it from the left side, like following a recipe that says which ingredient goes where.

### Question 38

If someone says no, write down that they said no and tell the person in charge; never pretend it happened or make them do it.

### Question 39

Make sure there is enough in the cup for the test, like making sure there is enough flour before you start baking.

### Question 40

It is like counting the cookies against the order at the end of the day to be sure none are missing or extra.

### Question 41

If a name tag is too messy to read, do not guess who it belongs to; get a fresh, clearly labeled sample.

### Question 42

If the name on the cup does not match the name on the paper, stop and tell an adult; do not change the names to make them match.

### Question 43

If two classmates share a name, you need their birthdays too, like using both name and birthday to tell the two people apart.

### Question 44

If you are not sure who someone is, do not take the sample yet; get help to make sure it is the right person.

### Question 45

If a sample has the wrong name tag, do not just switch the tag; start over with a fresh sample labeled the right way.

### Question 46

If the sample looks spoiled, tell someone so it can be done again, instead of sending something that will not work.

### Question 47

If the sample cannot be given right now, tell the doctor so they can decide what to do, and write down what happened.

### Question 48

If the sample got dirty along the way, it is better to explain again and get a clean one than to send the dirty one.

### Question 49

If you are not trained to do a job safely, say so and get someone who is, instead of trying it and risking harm.

### Question 50

If you get poked by a used needle, wash it with soap and water right away and tell a grown-up in charge immediately.

### Question 51

If something splashes in your eye or mouth, rinse it with water right away and tell the person in charge, even if the patient seems healthy.

### Question 52

If something spills, clean it up the safe way with gloves and the right cleaner, like cleaning up a broken egg without touching the mess with bare hands.

### Question 53

If the sample sat out too long, tell someone so they can decide if it is still good or needs to be done again.

### Question 54

If the fridge is too warm, tell the person in charge right away, like telling someone the freezer door was left open.

### Question 55

If someone starts to feel faint, help them sit or lie down, call for help, and stay with them until they feel better.

### Question 56

If an important message comes in, deliver it to the right person quickly; do not try to explain it yourself.

### Question 57

When someone asks what their test means, pass the question to the doctor, who is the right person to explain it.

### Question 58

If the record says a sample was taken but it is gone, tell someone so they can find it or redo it; do not hide it.

### Question 59

If you see someone touching samples without gloves, speak up and tell the person in charge, because gloves keep everyone safe.

### Question 60

Never put the cap back on with two hands; drop the used needle straight into the special sharps box so nobody gets poked.

### Question 61

Used needles go in the special hard box with the sharp warning, never in the normal trash where they could poke someone.

### Question 62

When you are stuck on a problem, tell your supervisor or the right teammate, like asking the teacher for help instead of hiding it.

### Question 63

If you make a mistake, tell someone right away so it can be fixed; hiding mistakes can hurt people.

### Question 64

When the sample is for someone who cannot decide for themselves, make sure the right permission and the right name are in place, and ask for help if unsure.

### Question 65

If you and the patient speak different languages, bring in an interpreter so both of you understand, like using a translator app to be sure of the directions.

### Question 66

If a sample was made at home, check the label and ask when and how it was collected; if unsure, tell someone before sending it.

### Question 67

If a supply has passed its use-by date, do not use it; set it aside and tell the person in charge.

### Question 68

If a cup is cracked, do not use it; tell someone so they can get more, and do not just skip the job.

### Question 69

The little warning sign means the stuff inside could carry germs, so handle it carefully with protection.

### Question 70

Once a needle is used, put it straight into the sharps box; do not fiddle with it.

### Question 71

If a sample must stay out of the light or the cold, follow that special rule, and ask if you are not sure what it is.

### Question 72

If you do not know the steps, ask someone who does; do not guess.

### Question 73

If a machine is broken, stop using it and tell someone who can fix it; do not keep using it or try to fix it yourself.

### Question 74

For very important samples, write down every single step of who had it, like keeping a careful log for something valuable.

### Question 75

Before a special sample is taken, make sure the right permission slip is signed and the rules are followed.

### Question 76

Do the steps in order: check the name, fill the cup, put the label on right away, double-check, write it down, then send it off.

### Question 77

If a sample breaks, clean it up safely and tell someone so a new sample can be collected.

### Question 78

If the patient was not told the prep steps, tell the doctor before collecting so the test is not messed up.

### Question 79

If an urgent sample is missing, tell someone right away so it can be found or redone quickly.

### Question 80

Never leave needles lying around or throw them in the normal bin, because someone could get poked.

### Question 81

If you are not sure whether a splash counts, tell the person in charge so they can check, instead of guessing.

### Question 82

Make sure the paper matches the right person and the doctor's request, like checking the order ticket before packing the box.

### Question 83

If the label machine is broken, write a clear, complete label by hand using the office's rules; never send a sample with no name.

### Question 84

Ask the person to say their full name and birthday themselves, like asking them to spell their name, instead of reading it and letting them just say yes.
